The NEVER-2 ledger, 2 legs (DEP the deploy, RB the read-backs), opened with its sentinel BEFORE the act and CLOSED with both proven and the sentinel removed. acceptance.status_reason: The act is not half-landed and the host runs the release this order cut. The issuer recorded the base as FAIL (0 entries, ap4_release.json absent, manifest still reading r29 91811b648a); all three moved. The criterion's own equality limb is the sharper half: it compares the MANIFEST's deployed_commit against the applier's independently written release_sha, so a manifest recorded from the wrong sha, or a release_sha invented after the fact, would read equal=no. WHAT AC1 DOES NOT COVER, and the order says so itself: the SERVED allowlist is OG-tl-1's AC2, not this criterion. AC1 proves the host runs these bytes; it does not prove the four meetings are now admitted on a real call, and I did not run the served read -- OG-tl-1's worker does that at Phase C and dell2's re-probe is the CVO's AC3. The strongest thing I can say about the served effect is CTO C1's measured key-set equality plus the value limb isolating TRANSCRIPT_MEETING_ALLOWLIST as the only value this deploy moved.

mutant.description: Readers were shown able to go both ways. (1) The issuer recorded the base as ap4.AC1 FAIL on three separate grounds and all three moved. (2) CTO C1 was MEASURED rather than eyeballed: the deploy's own ENV_KEYS_BEFORE and ENV_KEYS_AFTER lines were parsed and compared as sets AND as ordered lists, with the missing-after and added-after sets printed -- so a lost key could not hide behind a matching count. (3) The value limb was run WIDE against the pre-r29 state, which means it had to name three changed values and did: a narrower window could have passed while silently tolerating a fourth. (4) The re-cut's equality was established by three independent measures (blob, patch-id, and a two-row git status), not one. (5) The halt gate had refused this same script twice earlier today under OG-ap-3, so its ability to say NO was already demonstrated; here the premise was made true at cut time and it said YES.
mutant.expected: AC1 moves FAIL -> PASS on all three of its grounds; the key-set comparison can distinguish a lost key; and the re-cut's equality is not asserted from a single measure.
mutant.observed: AC1 PASS with entries 1, CLOSED, sentinel absent, equal=yes. ENV_KEYS 52 vs 52, set equal and list equal, missing NONE, added NONE. Value limb equal 48 of 51 with exactly the three expected names. Blob, patch-id and status all independently exact. MainPID moved 857046 -> 862375, the positive evidence the service actually restarted.

determinism.method: Every world read came from an instrument separate from the act: the issuer's ap4.AC1.sh, the deploy script's own ENV_KEYS lines, and r29_verify.py's host reads over SSM. The re-cut was measured against the ORIGINAL release's blobs and patch-id rather than against my own output. The deploy ran from a worktree that stayed at the re-cut commit with a clean tree throughout.
determinism.observed: The manifest's deployed_commit and the applier's release_sha agree (ap4.AC1), and both agree with the worktree's HEAD. The shipped md5 reads 98 of 98 against the r29 release list, which is correct precisely because the allowlist json is read laptop-side and is not a shipped file -- so the shipped set is unchanged by this release and its md5 should NOT have moved.

declared_exclusions.item: A before-state captured for THIS deploy alone.
declared_exclusions.reason: NOT captured, and named rather than hidden. r29_verify.py's before mode saves a state file and I had only the pre-r29 one. Instead of a narrow window I ran the value comparison WIDE against that state with three expected-changed names, which establishes 'only TRANSCRIPT_MEETING_ALLOWLIST moved here' by subtraction across BOTH deploys -- a stronger claim than the narrow one, reached because the narrow one was unavailable. A future applier should capture a before-state per deploy so the direct check is also available.

Worth noting for the next row filed under this order: its declared id form NFRA_OPLGTW-Z-AE-S<k> would be REFUSED by surprise-row-gate.py's ID_RE, which admits only ONE optional segment of a letter plus digits ('-Z-AE-' is two). The same class the MX-s-19 A3 amendment ruled when it retired 'Z-AEMI-', and the same one I hit on NFRA_IAMROLES202609's '-Z-AEC-' earlier today. Recorded here because it costs a refusal round-trip at the moment someone has a finding to file.

session_log: This seat is a SESSION seat, not an L7 worker subagent. GO: 2.0.0_SA_COO~O msg 32794 with amendment A1 @2b6e55bfed, which re-sequenced this ahead of NFRA_MCPORTAL MP-x-4 and turned step 0's precondition off. Order of acts was the order's own. Two things went better here than they did two orders earlier, and both are the same lesson applied forward. First, the halt gate passed FIRST TIME: OG-ap-3 cost three deploy attempts because a sparse worktree did not materialise this seat's agent home, and the gate reads HALT_GATE_REPO_ROOT alone; here I cut a FULL worktree, verified the agent home was present at creation, and dry-ran the gate with the root safe-ec2-deploy.sh:57 actually pins before touching the host. Second, the re-cut's exactness was established BEFORE applying rather than discovered after: comparing the live ref's blob against the reference hunk's pre-image index showed they were identical, which is why the patch-id could not drift and why the COO half's condition was satisfiable at all. CTO C1 was measured by parsing the deploy's own ENV_KEYS lines and comparing them as sets and as ordered lists, not by reading two long lines side by side. One gap is named rather than papered over: no before-state was captured for this deploy alone, so the value check was run wide against the pre-r29 state and the claim is made by subtraction across both deploys. One commit attempt was REFUSED mid-way because a peer's merge was in progress in the shared tree; I did not resolve or abort another seat's merge, measured that MERGE_HEAD and the conflict set were clear moments later, and retried. Nothing was pushed.
